subject: Episilon Health - request for temporary log archival and SIG evidence
messages:
From: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@episilonhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 90-day retention for audit window + SIG artifacts

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this. We have an upcoming compliance-driven review tied to a third-party forensic request covering patient-access logs for a specific workflow. Our auditors require access to application-level request logs for a 90-day window (currently Redwood default is 30 days).

Can Redwood do a temporary archival/hold for Episilon tenant logs for the window 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-30 and supply SIG/CAIQ extracts that show retention controls, access controls, and encryption-at-rest details? Our security team also asked for a brief statement of how access to archived logs will be limited and audited.

If possible, please outline the operational steps, any cost or contract amendment needed, and estimated timeline. We may need a signed addendum.

Apologies for the short notice — our external auditor moved the review up. Let me know what you need from our side.

Thanks,
Adrian Cole
Sr. IT Compliance Manager
Episilon Health
adrian.cole@episilonhealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

[Attachment: initial-audit-scope.pdf (pdf)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@episilonhealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: 90-day retention for audit window + SIG artifacts

Hi Adrian —

Thanks for the heads up and the scope doc. We can support a targeted temporary retention/hold for tenant-level request logs, but there are a few moving parts to confirm:

- Scope: narrow hold to the tenant and time window you specified (2026-05-01 to 2026-07-30). Please confirm there are no additional environments.
- Evidence: we can provide a SIG extract showing control mappings and a CAIQ snapshot for storage/retention controls; I will route to Security for the detailed extract.
- Controls for access: archived logs will be stored encrypted with KMS, access limited to a small list of authorized engineers/forensics on a need-to-know basis, and all accesses will be logged.
- Timeline & approvals: we need Security approval + Legal sign-off for a one-time amendment; typical turnaround is 5-7 business days after we have the signed exception form.

Please find attached a blank retention-exception form that we use to capture scope and authorization. If you can fill and return it I will start the internal approval flow right away.

Proposed next steps:
1) Episilon returns the completed retention-exception form and confirms the exact tenant id(s).
2) Redwood Security produces SIG/CAIQ extracts and confirms technical storage approach.
3) Legal issues a short contract amendment for signatures.

Dylan (CC) will help with estimates on cost and logistics.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

[Attachment: episilon-retention-exception-form.xlsx]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Episilon Health - request for temporary log archival and SIG evidence

Team — forwarding request from Episilon Health (external). Short summary and my proposed approach below.

Summary: External auditor needs 90-day tenant logs for a time window we normally don't retain. Customer asks for SIG/CAIQ extracts + statement of access limitations. They expect an amendment and a one-off archival/hold.

Proposed plan (operations + controls):
- Scope: retain application request logs for tenant "epsl-prod-43" only for 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-30, then schedule secure purge after 180 days unless otherwise extended.
- Access controls: create a temporary IAM group with MFA, restrict to SRE forensics and Security; require ticketed approval for each retrieval; all accesses logged and cross-referenced to JIRA ticket.
- Storage: encrypt with customer-managed KMS key (if customer wants); otherwise Redwood-managed KMS with CMEK tag and key rotation logs provided.
- Evidence to deliver: SIG extract answers (control mappings), CAIQ snapshot for storage/retention, proof of encryption-at-rest, and an access log sample showing retrieval gating.
- Legal: one-page amendment consistent with prior exception flows; propose that Episilon signs a 1-time addendum accepting the extra charge.

Risks/notes: this is scoped and time-bound. If we expand scope (multiple tenants, longer windows) we should escalate to ops/finance for pricing.

Questions for Security and Legal:
- Stephanie: is the above controls list sufficient or do you require additional safeguards?
- Marissa: do we have a standard addendum template we can reuse for this type of retention exception?

Attachments: I drafted a filled example of the exception form and an audit-window spec doc (attached).

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround; customer timeline is tight.

— Lauren

Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Episilon Health - request for temporary log archival and SIG evidence

Lauren — thanks for the clear write-up and proposed controls. From a Security side we can approve the temporary archival under the following conditions:

1) Narrow scope verification: we must receive the exact tenant id(s) and a signed retention-exception form from Episilon confirming the audit scope.
2) Access gating: retrievals require a JIRA ticket, two-person approval (Security + SRE on-call), and are time-limited (we'll create 12-hour access windows).
3) Encryption: if Episilon requests CMEK we will onboard the key; otherwise Redwood-managed KMS with exported evidence (key metadata and rotation log) is acceptable.
4) Audit trail: provide a sample access log and the list of user principals who will have retrieval privileges.
5) One-time retention window: we will store the archived logs for 180 days post-archive, after which an automated purge will run unless Episilon sends a written extension request.

Deliverables we will prepare once the completed form arrives:
- SIG extract (answers subset relevant to retention & access) — see attached sample.
- CAIQ snapshot for storage controls.
- Short ops runbook describing retrieval procedure and approval flow.

Marissa — Legal can we reuse the 2025 retention amendment template? If yes, I suggest we prefill with the scope and cost estimate and send DocuSign link to the customer.

If everyone agrees I will start the technical steps once the form and tenant id are in.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Attachments: SIG-extract-answers.pdf, retention-amendment-template.docx
